items.goal: Add a 'Back to top' link to the WebApp footer's bottom row, next to the legal links, that scrolls the current page to its top (header visible) without leaving the page.
items.modelReason: Small markup change in one component, plus one id on the header.

The footer is static SSR; making it interactive adds a circuit for a single link.

subject: test-planner
reason: Split by acceptance criterion: link presence on two page types (AC1), scroll-to-top on catalog page 1 plus the page-2 query-string boundary that the base href could break (AC2), and two regression cases pinning the footer columns and the bottom row (AC3).

items.title: Catalog page footer shows "Back to top" as the last legal link
covers: AC1: footer bottom row shows a Back to top link next to the legal links
items.reason: AC1 requires the link in the footer's bottom row next to the legal links; the Implementation Notes put it as the last item of the `Legal` list. If it were missing or placed elsewhere, shoppers would not find it. Only a rendered page in a browser shows this, so the case is e2e.

items.title: Item page footer shows "Back to top" next to the legal links
covers: AC1: Given any page of the store
items.reason: AC1 says "any page of the store", not only the catalog; the footer is in the shared layout, and this case proves it on a second, routed page with a path parameter. A separate case keeps the catalog check (TC-PRB-8-01) independent of item data.

items.title: Clicking "Back to top" at the bottom of the catalog scrolls to the top and shows the header on the same page
covers: AC2: page scrolled to its top
items.reason: This is the story's core behaviour (AC2). The Implementation Notes record two traps: the sticky header never counts as out of view, and `<base href="/">` can redirect a bare fragment; a regression in either leaves the page unscrolled or navigates away. Only a real browser scroll shows it, so the case is e2e.

items.title: "Back to top" on catalog page 2 keeps the shopper on page 2 instead of the home page
covers: Implementation Notes: href is current base-relative URI plus #top
items.reason: AC2 says the click must not leave the page. With `<base href="/">`, a bare `#top` resolves to `/#top`, which from a catalog page with a query string (`?page=2`) would drop the shopper back on page 1. Page 1 at `/` cannot reveal that bug because `/#top` is the same page, so this boundary needs its own case.

items.title: Footer link columns, brand and social links are unchanged
covers: AC3: the footer's other links are unchanged
items.reason: AC3 forbids side effects on the rest of the footer. Pinning the existing links and their targets catches an accidental edit while adding the new item. It is separate from TC-PRB-8-06 because the columns and the bottom row are different regions that can break independently.

items.title: Copyright line and Privacy, Terms, Cookies legal links are unchanged
covers: AC3: the copyright line is unchanged
AC3: the legal links are unchanged
items.reason: The new link is inserted into the same list as the legal links (Implementation Notes), so the legal links and the copyright line beside them are the most likely to be disturbed. AC3 requires them unchanged.
